translation: Now the kidney water belongs to yin and is originally cold; when deficient it becomes heat. The heart fire belongs to yang and is originally hot; when deficient it becomes cold. If the kidney water is yin-deficient, then the heart fire is yang-excess; this is called yang-excess and yin-deficiency, and both upper and lower are hot—this is clear. Therefore the Qi Jue Lun (氣厥論) says: When the kidney qi declines, yang qi alone prevails. The Xuanming Wu Qi Lun (宣明五氣論) says: The kidney dislikes dryness; because of dryness, the kidney withers and the water dries up.
translator_notes: 氣厥論/宣明五氣論 kept as chapter names; 腎水/心火 rendered 'kidney water'/'heart fire'.
